timing_gold.source: observed — D7, MuckRock's own aggregate statistic across all MuckRock-tracked requests to the Los Angeles Police Department, scraped 2026-09-15. Statutory ceiling for comparison is 24 days (10 + 14).
timing_gold.quote: All four agencies' MuckRock-observed average response times (83-157 days) are 3.5x to 6.5x longer than the statutory maximum of 24 days (10-day determination + 14-day 'unusual circumstances' extension under Gov. Code SS7922.535).
timing_gold.n_requests: MuckRock aggregate, count not published on the agency page; 3 individual LAPD request timelines inspected (D8)
timing_gold.note: 150 days is a MuckRock mean, not a median, and it pools every request type MuckRock users filed with LAPD. The per-request sample (D8) is bimodal rather than centred: nothing in it resolved near 24 days, while two requests have been open 19 months and 2 years respectively with nothing released.

known_gaps: The triage decision itself. The manual specifies the extension grounds, the exemption menu, and the escalation chain, but nothing — statute, manual, or observed data — states the criteria an analyst actually uses to decide that a request is the kind that gets serially deferred. The CHP roster request resolved in 28 days; the LAPD ALPR request was re-deferred nine times over 19+ months. The mechanism is fully visible; the selection rule is not.

Whether serial re-extension is authorised at all. §7922.535(b) caps a single notice at 14 days and the manual says no other reasons justify an extension, yet the observed practice is an indefinitely renewable rolling deferral. No document collected reconciles the two, and nothing short of litigation enforces the cap.

How long each internal segment takes. The manual names the analyst assignment, the division search, the employee personal-account search, the supervisor consult and the City Attorney escalation but attaches no service level to any of them; the only number anywhere is the 10/24-day statutory one.

No denial rate is published. MuckRock reports a 31.90% success rate for LAPD, which is not the complement of a denial rate (it pools withdrawals, abandonment, no-records outcomes and requests still open).

Volume and staffing. Nothing states how many CPRA requests LAPD receives, how many analysts the CPRA Unit has, or what the queue looks like — so the 150-day average cannot be decomposed into queueing versus review time.

Upstream record retention. A records-retention practice that destroys records before any request arrives (A23's lawful destruction path, and the reported use of auto-deleting chat tools elsewhere in the City) defeats a request invisibly; the manual acknowledges destruction as a denial ground but no document quantifies it.
Fee practice. The manual restates the direct-cost-of-duplication rule but there is no LAPD fee schedule in the corpus; the only figure is MuckRock's observed $35.03 average.
notes: The LAPD CPRA Unit Manual v11 is a genuine internal staff manual, found on a public Azure Government Cloud blob URL with no access control, and it is fully updated to the 2023 §7920.000-series numbering — while the City's own applicant-facing page (D6) still cites the superseded §6250/§6253(c)/§6252(e) numbering. That mismatch is the sharpest declared-vs-designed seam in this slug and is the reason the statutory element_refs in this model use the current numbering even though a solver reading only the City page would produce the old one. Visibility calls: the analyst assignment (A05) and the SB 1421/16 sub-workflow (A17) are marked applicant_inferable rather than staff_only because the MuckRock request logs show the requester being told both; A07, A08, A10, A14, A15, A18 and A19 appear in no applicant-facing document held in raw/ and are marked staff_only. A08 (pushing the request out to employees' personal devices and relying on them to self-search) and A19 (the five-rung legal-advice escalation chain) are the two activities a solver working from the public page could not reach by any route. Sibling processes deliberately excluded: federal FOIA (which nine reddit posts in this corpus conflate with CPRA), Pitchess motions, and subpoena responses — the same PRSR Section handles subpoenas, but that is not a CPRA path.
